label: proof
title: Quantitative sufficient condition for transferring a leaf-sum CLT
statement: Let X_n and Y_n be integrable sums of n leaf scores on one coupled probability space. Suppose every corresponding score differs in absolute value by at most epsilon_n, and sqrt(n)*epsilon_n tends to zero. If (Y_n-E Y_n)/sqrt(n) converges in distribution to N(0,sigma^2), then (X_n-E X_n)/sqrt(n) has the same limit. In particular, a sufficient quantitative locality condition is a coupling of finite-tree scores to the stationary scores with uniform score error o(n^(-1/2)).
proof_text: The pathwise sum difference is bounded by n*epsilon_n and the difference of the expectations by the same quantity. Hence the absolute difference of the centered normalized sums is at most 2*sqrt(n)*epsilon_n, which tends to zero. For any real x and eta>0, their distribution functions are squeezed between the distribution function of the Y sum at x-eta and x+eta for all sufficiently large n. Continuity of the Gaussian distribution function proves the assertion, including a constant limit by the usual convergence-in-probability version. This is an explicit transfer criterion, not a proof that the beta-splitting model supplies the coupling.
assumptions: Integrable scores and a common coupling
A deterministic uniform per-score error bound
sqrt(n)*epsilon_n -> 0
limitations: No such coupling or error bound has been proved here for DTCS(n). A stationary CLT and qualitative local convergence alone do not provide it.

label: proof
title: Three fluctuation regimes for the earlier retained-root perturbation
statement: Assume finite binary trees retain an identifiable original degree-two root after leaf rerooting, and their ordered root split law is q_n(i)=n/(2 H_(n-1) i(n-i)), 1<=i<n. Let B_n indicate min(i,n-i)<=floor(sqrt(n)), let p_n=E B_n, and give every leaf the same score f_a=n^(-a)(B_n-p_n), with score zero on infinite trees and a>0. The finite centered score sum divided by sqrt(n) is n^(1/2-a)(B_n-p_n). It is not tight for 0<a<1/2, converges to a two-point law at a=1/2, and tends uniformly to zero for a>1/2. Every infinite-tree score is zero.
proof_text: For n>=9 put k=floor(sqrt(n))<n/2. Since q_n(i)=(1/i+1/(n-i))/(2 H_(n-1)), symmetry gives p_n=(H_k+H_(n-1)-H_(n-k-1))/H_(n-1). The first numerator term is (1/2) log n+O(1), and the other difference is at most k/(n-k)=O(n^(-1/2)); H_(n-1)=log n+O(1). Thus p_n ->1/2. Both possible values of B_n-p_n have absolute value approaching 1/2. Multiplication by n^(1/2-a) gives the three stated regimes. The scores have expectation zero exactly. On bounded-degree trees with the retained-root topology, every finite tree is isolated locally, while convergence to an infinite tree forces the leaf count to diverge. Therefore |f_a|<=n^(-a) proves continuity at infinite trees. This generalizes the earlier a=1/4 obstruction; it does not verify the retained-root assumption in the original problem's precise topology.
assumptions: The original degree-two root is retained and identifiable
The displayed critical root-split law
The local topology and score domain retain that root
limitations: This is a conditional topology-specific obstruction with a degenerate infinite CLT. It is not a checked solution of Open Problem 12. A concrete nondegenerate beta-splitting counterexample remains open in this packet.

label: proof
title: Discovery from a divergent conditional survival compensator
statement: Let T>=1 be an integer-valued stopping time for a filtration (F_n), possibly infinite, and set p_n=E[1_{T=n+1}|F_n] and A_m=sum_(n<m) p_n. Then P(T=infinity and A_infinity=infinity)=0. For countably many targets this implies almost sure discovery of all targets if each target's compensator diverges on its never-discovered event outside a null set. Divergence is a sufficient condition, not a necessary one.
proof_text: Because p_n=0 after T, Z_m=1_{T>m} exp(A_m) is a nonnegative supermartingale with Z_0=1: its conditional next expectation is Z_m*(1-p_m)*exp(p_m)<=Z_m. For K>0 stop at sigma_K=inf{m:A_m>=K}. Bounded optional stopping at sigma_K wedge r gives P(sigma_K<=r,T>sigma_K)<=exp(-K). Let r increase, and then K increase, to obtain the result. The countable-target conclusion follows by a countable union of null sets. If deterministic a_n in [0,1] satisfy p_n>=a_n on {T>n}, the direct recursion P(T>n+1)<= (1-a_n)P(T>n) gives the product tail bound and hence P(T>m)<=exp(-sum_(n<m)a_n). For a_n=c/(n+1), 0<c<=1, this is at most (m+1)^(-c). Necessity fails when T=1 deterministically, since A_infinity=1 although discovery is certain.
assumptions: T is a stopping time relative to the actual exploration history
p_n are actual target-specific conditional probabilities
The countable application verifies divergence separately on each survival event
limitations: For filled-in peeling, the lower bound by a perimeter-only q(S_n) and the divergence for all critical weight sequences are still required. The earlier unreviewed equivalence is not imported as a theorem.

label: proof
title: Exact finite-time expansion in the annular Skorokhod problem
statement: For the smooth bounded connected annulus D={x in R^2:1<|x|<3}, normal reflection driven by w(t)=(-t,0) can increase the distance of two synchronously driven paths. Start X(0)=(1,0) and Y(0)=(cos(theta),sin(theta)), 0<theta<pi/2. Until t<log(cot(theta/2)), X(t)=(1,0) and Y(t)=(cos(phi(t)),sin(phi(t))) with phi(t)=2 arctan(exp(t)tan(theta/2)); the squared distance has derivative 2 sin(phi(t))^2>0.
proof_text: On the inner circle the inward normal of the annulus is the outward radial vector. For X, take reflection regulator L_X(t)=t, so dX=(-1,0)dt+(1,0)dL_X=0. For Y, choose dL_Y=cos(phi)dt, which is nonnegative while phi<pi/2. The Skorokhod equation then gives Y'=(-1,0)+cos(phi)(cos(phi),sin(phi))=(-sin(phi)^2,cos(phi)sin(phi)). This equals (-sin(phi),cos(phi))*phi' when phi'=sin(phi), and the displayed solution solves that ODE. Both regulators increase only on the inner boundary, both paths stay in the closed annulus, and neither reaches the outer boundary. Their squared distance is 2(1-cos(phi)), with derivative 2 sin(phi)^2. This is a complete deterministic calculation.
assumptions: Deterministic continuous finite-variation driving path
Normal Skorokhod reflection on the closed annulus
Boundary starting points and 0<theta<pi/2
0<=t<log(cot(theta/2))
limitations: Finite-time deterministic expansion is compatible with eventual Brownian contraction. The cached author page excludes one-hole domains as long-term counterexamples (see one-hole-exclusion-source-restriction.md). No positive long-time limsup is established.

label: proof
title: Logarithmic city-count lower bound under the earlier founding-rate estimate
statement: Let (M_t) be an adapted nondecreasing integer process, t>=1, with M_1>=1, whose increments are zero or one. Suppose P(M_(t+1)=M_t+1|F_t)>=1/[2(1+K*t*M_t^d)] for constants K>0,d>=0. Then constants kappa,c>0 exist such that, for all large integer t, P(M_t<floor(kappa*(log t)^(1/(d+1))))<=exp(-c*(log t)^(1/(d+1))). Moreover almost surely liminf M_t/(log t)^(1/(d+1))>0. For the verified alpha=1, beta>0 city model, d=max(beta/2-1,0), giving exponent min(1,2/beta).
proof_text: Set m=floor(kappa*(log t)^(1/(d+1)))>=1. Before M reaches m, the founding chance at step s is at least a_s=1/[2(1+K*s*m^d)]>=1/[2(1+K)*s*m^d] for s>=1. Using independent uniforms to realize the adapted Bernoulli increments, compare with independent Bernoulli(a_s) variables until the threshold; after the threshold extend the comparison success variables arbitrarily. If M_t<m then the threshold was never reached, so the sum B of comparison successes from s=1 to t-1 is smaller than m. Its mean mu is at least H_(t-1)/[2(1+K)*m^d]. Choose kappa so kappa^(d+1)<=1/[16(1+K)]. For large t the harmonic sum is at least (log t)/2, implying mu>=4m and mu is bounded below by a positive multiple of (log t)^(1/(d+1)). The Chernoff lower-tail bound P(B<=mu/2)<=exp(-mu/8) proves the probability assertion. For the almost sure statement use t_j=ceil(exp(j^(d+1))) and sum the bounds exp(-c*j). Borel-Cantelli gives the lower bound eventually on these times. Monotonicity of M_t and log(t_(j+1))/log(t_j)->1 interpolate it to all large t.
assumptions: Adapted city-count process with increments in {0,1}
The displayed conditional founding-rate bound at every step
K>0 and d>=0
limitations: The primary model definition and the spatial founding-rate bound are checked in max-influence-city-founding-rate.md, so the lemma supplies an almost-sure lower bound for the alpha=1, beta>0 Aldous-Huang model. It gives no matching upper bound or comparable city populations.

label: proof
title: Conditional deep-level law from truncated marked-Poisson moments
statement: Fix alpha>0 and z>=0 finite. Let heights h_i form a Poisson process on R of intensity z*exp(-alpha*h) dh, carrying independent identically distributed measurable nonnegative marks K_i(s), s>=0, independent of the heights. Suppose exp(-alpha*s)*E K(s)->c in (0,infinity) and E K(s)^2<=C*exp(2*alpha*s) for every s>=0. Set S_t=sum_(h_i>=-t) K_i(t+h_i). Then S_t/(t*exp(alpha*t))->c*z in probability as t->infinity. The same conclusion holds with a finite almost-sure random intensity Z conditionally on Z and unconditionally, without assuming E Z<infinity. This is a conditional criterion for the limiting DGFF cluster process, not a proof of its moment hypotheses or the finite-N limit.
proof_text: For a fixed upper cutoff H and t+H>=0 define S_t^H using -t<=h_i<=H. Poisson integration and the change of variable s=t+h give E S_t^H=z*exp(alpha*t)*integral_0^(t+H) exp(-alpha*s)*E K(s) ds. Cesaro averaging implies this divided by t*exp(alpha*t) tends to c*z. Its variance divided by t^2*exp(2*alpha*t) is at most z*C*exp(alpha*H)/(alpha*t^2), so the truncated variable converges in L2 for fixed H. The probability that the full and truncated sums differ is at most the probability of any height above H, namely 1-exp(-z*exp(-alpha*H)/alpha). First send t to infinity, then H to infinity, to prove convergence in probability. For random finite Z, these conditional error probabilities tend to zero and are bounded by one, so dominated convergence applies; E Z is not required. For finitely many disjoint spatial sets the same argument and a finite union bound give joint convergence with their respective intensity masses. Notice that E S_t is infinite whenever z>0 under the stated first-moment asymptotic: its integral extends over s in [0,infinity). Thus full-sum L2 convergence or uniform integrability must not be silently assumed. The earlier intake integral with exp(+alpha*s) inside reverses the change-of-variable sign.
assumptions: A marked Poisson process with the stated intensity and independent identically distributed decorations
alpha>0 and finite z (or a.s. finite random Z)
The two explicit first and second decoration moment hypotheses
limitations: The moment hypotheses and the exchange or iterated use of the finite-N and deep-level limits are not verified for DGFF. The full limiting sum can have infinite expectation even while its normalized values converge in probability.

label: proof
title: The recorded derivative inequality does not imply susceptibility divergence
statement: The implications theta(delta)~delta and theta'(delta)<=C*chi(delta), even with theta,chi positive and smooth on 0<delta<1, do not imply chi(delta)>=c/delta for any c>0. Therefore the earlier C0065 attempt's claimed inverse-distance lower bound does not follow from the two displayed premises. This refutes that inference, not the percolation lower bound itself.
proof_text: Take theta(delta)=delta, chi(delta)=1 and C=1. Then theta'(delta)=1<=C*chi(delta), and theta(delta)/delta=1 exactly. However delta*chi(delta)=delta->0, so no positive c can satisfy chi(delta)>=c/delta for all sufficiently small delta. Both functions meet the stated smoothness and positivity requirements. Extra percolation inequalities could still prove a susceptibility lower bound, but they are additional premises and are not supplied by this derivative comparison.
assumptions: Only the two derivative-and-order premises quoted in the earlier attempt are being tested
limitations: No claim is made that the actual high-dimensional finite-cluster susceptibility has this counterexample behavior. The claimed percolation theorem must be re-proved from valid percolation-specific inputs.

label: proof
title: Exact supercritical finite susceptibility on the degree-three tree
statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on the infinite degree-three tree, 1/2<p<1, write chi_f(p)=E_p[|C_o|*1_{|C_o|<infinity}]. Then chi_f(p)=((1-p)/p)^3*(2-p)/(2*p-1), and (p-1/2)*chi_f(p)->3/4 as p decreases to 1/2. Below criticality chi(p)=(1+p)/(1-2*p), with (1/2-p)*chi(p)->3/4. Thus the finite-susceptibility exponents agree and equal one on this tree.
proof_text: Let t be the probability that a directed edge does not lead to infinity. Independence of the two forward branches gives t=1-p+p*t^2; the smaller root for p>1/2 is t=(1-p)/p. The root cluster is finite exactly when all three outward edge branches fail, an event of probability t^3. Conditional on such failure, each edge is open and has a finite forward subtree with probability r=p*t^2/t=p*t=1-p. The finite cluster therefore has root offspring Binomial(3,r), then Binomial(2,r) offspring thereafter. The mean total size conditional on finiteness is 1+3*r/(1-2*r)=(2-p)/(2*p-1). Multiplication by t^3 proves the formula and the limit. For p<1/2 all branches die, and the same offspring computation with r=p gives the subcritical formula.
assumptions: The infinite degree-three tree
Independent Bernoulli bond percolation
Susceptibility uses the unconditioned finite-cluster first moment
limitations: This is a branching-tree special case. It proves neither the high-dimensional lattice result nor the spatial correlation-length exponents; graph distance on a tree has different geometry.

label: proof
title: Finite weight means fix the annealed one-edge decay exponent
statement: Let iid positive weights W_x have finite mean mu, and conditionally independent edges have probability 1-exp(-lambda*W_x*W_y*|x-y|^(-b)), with b,lambda>0. Then the annealed one-edge probability is asymptotic to lambda*mu^2*|x-y|^(-b) as |x-y|->infinity. In particular for Pareto weights P(W>w)=w^(-rho), w>=1, rho>1, its coefficient is lambda*(rho/(rho-1))^2. A tail exponent b*rho cannot be inferred for this finite-mean regime from the weight-tail parameter.
proof_text: Set V=W_x*W_y and s=lambda*|x-y|^(-b). For V>=0, 0<=(1-exp(-s*V))/s<=V, and the expression tends pointwise to V as s decreases to zero. Independence and the finite weight mean give E V=mu^2<infinity. Dominated convergence yields the asymptotic. For a Pareto variable the density rho*w^(-rho-1) on w>=1 gives E W=rho/(rho-1). This is an edge-probability calculation; it does not compute the connectedness two-point function or a critical exponent.
assumptions: Independent identically distributed positive weights with finite mean
The displayed conditional edge law
Fixed positive b and lambda
limitations: The annealed one-edge probability is different from the annealed connectedness function. No mean-field boundary, critical dimension or continuity of theta is deduced.

label: proof
title: Shared vertex weights strictly correlate annealed adjacent edges
statement: In the same scale-free edge model, take three distinct vertices 0,1,2, independent positive weights, and positive edge coefficients a,b. Let I_01 and I_02 be their edge indicators, conditionally independent given all weights. Then Cov(I_01,I_02)=Cov(g_a(W_0),g_b(W_0)), where g_a(w)=E[1-exp(-a*w*W_1)]. This covariance is positive when W_0 is nondegenerate. Thus an independent-edge model with the same edge marginals already disagrees on two-edge events.
proof_text: Given W_0, integrating the independent endpoint weights leaves I_01 and I_02 independent Bernoulli variables with parameters g_a(W_0) and g_b(W_0), respectively. Conditional covariance is zero, so the covariance identity follows by conditioning. Each g is strictly increasing because the other weights are positive almost surely. For an independent copy W_0', covariance equals one half of E[(g_a(W_0)-g_a(W_0'))*(g_b(W_0)-g_b(W_0'))]. The integrand is nonnegative everywhere and strictly positive on {W_0!=W_0'}, which has positive probability for a nondegenerate distribution. All quantities are bounded and hence integrable, even for infinite-mean weights.
assumptions: Independent positive vertex weights
Conditional edge independence
Positive edge coefficients
Nondegenerate shared weight for strict positivity
limitations: This invalidates direct substitution by independent edges at the level of joint laws. It does not rule out proving suitable stochastic comparisons or universality by a separate argument.

label: proof
title: Exponential infinite-cluster contact tail on every regular tree above criticality
statement: On the (b+1)-regular tree with b>=2, independent Bernoulli bond percolation at fixed p in (1/b,1), there are constants C,c>0 such that P_p(|C_o|<infinity and J_o>n)<=C*exp(-c*n), where J_o counts all graph edges from C_o to vertices in any infinite open cluster. The assertion also holds trivially at p=1.
proof_text: Let t in (0,1) be the smaller solution of t=1-p+p*t^b. The root cluster is finite with probability t^(b+1). Conditional on finiteness, each outward edge opens into a finite branch with probability r=p*t^(b-1); this gives root offspring Binomial(b+1,r) and later offspring Binomial(b,r), independently. Strict convexity of f(x)=1-p+p*x^b-x, with roots t and 1, gives f'(t)<0, hence b*r<1. The forward progeny equation is F=z*(1-r+r*F)^b. The analytic implicit function theorem at (z,F)=(1,1), whose derivative in F is 1-b*r>0, gives a positive fixed point F_*(z)>1 for some z>1 sufficiently close to one. In fact F_*(z)>=z. The generating functions of generation-truncated progeny start at F_0(z)=z and satisfy F_(m+1)(z)=z*(1-r+r*F_m(z))^b. They increase and are bounded above by F_*(z), by induction. Monotone convergence then proves that the full progeny has a finite exponential moment at this z. The root-size generating function is z*(1-r+r*F(z))^(b+1), also finite. Markov's inequality gives an exponential tail for the finite cluster size. A finite connected tree with N vertices has exactly (b-1)*N+2 boundary edges by the degree sum, so J_o<=(b-1)*N+2. This transfers the size bound to J_o, with constants depending on b,p. At p=1 the finite-cluster event is empty.
assumptions: A regular tree of degree b+1, integer b>=2
Independent Bernoulli bond percolation
Fixed p>1/b
Contacts count graph edges, which must be closed at a finite open-cluster boundary
limitations: This does not give the requested estimate on arbitrary transitive graphs. The constants deteriorate toward criticality; no uniform rate in p is asserted.

label: proof
title: Quantitative hemisphere containment at a Holder differentiable boundary
statement: Suppose a domain near a boundary point z is, in coordinates with outward unit normal e_d, contained in {x_d<g(x')}, with g(0)=0 and |g(x')|<=C*|x'|^(1+gamma), gamma>0. For any interior x approaching z=0, its normalized approach vector u=(z-x)/|z-x| satisfies e_d dot u>=-C*|z-x|^gamma. Consequently every limiting approach direction lies in the closed outward hemisphere. This applies pathwise to Brownian exits at such points.
proof_text: Write r=|x|. Because x_d<=g(x')<=C*|x'|^(1+gamma)<=C*r^(1+gamma), the outward component of u=-x/r is -x_d/r>=-C*r^gamma. Let r decrease to zero along any convergent sequence of directions. The error vanishes, giving e_d dot u>=0. This is a deterministic local boundary statement, so continuity of a Brownian exit path is the only stochastic ingredient in this containment conclusion.
assumptions: A local boundary graph at the exit point with the displayed remainder bound
The orientation e_d is outward
Interior points approach that boundary point
limitations: Containment does not establish that every hemisphere direction occurs. Arbitrary nonsmooth domains need not have the displayed boundary graph.

label: proof
title: Invariant ergodic spanning forests can have every finite component count
statement: For each integer k>=2, the Cayley graph G_k of Z with generators {+1,-1,+k,-k} has a deterministic translation-invariant spanning forest with exactly k components. Keep exactly the length-k edges. Its point-mass law is ergodic under translations. Thus translation invariance and ergodicity alone cannot exclude any finite component count greater than one.
proof_text: Each retained component is one residue class modulo k, with edges between consecutive elements of that class. It is a bi-infinite path and hence has no cycle. Every integer belongs to exactly one of these k residue classes, so the forest spans G_k and has k components. Translation by one permutes the classes and preserves the whole edge set, proving invariance. A point-mass probability measure assigns every measurable event probability zero or one, and is therefore ergodic. The earlier k=2 example is its first instance. None of these deterministic forests is asserted to be a free uniform spanning forest.
assumptions: k is an integer at least two
G_k has both length-one and length-k edges
Only length-k edges are retained
limitations: This refutes a proposed inference from ergodicity, not the one-or-infinity classification for the actual FUSF law. It adds no nonunimodular FUSF counterexample.

label: proof
title: Certain discovery with a finite stopped-hazard sum
statement: For a target discovered at time T=1 deterministically, p_n=P(T=n+1|F_n) equals one at n=0 and zero thereafter. Thus discovery has probability one, while sum_n p_n=1 is finite. This refutes a general necessity claim for the actual stopped target hazard. It does not refute a perimeter-only equivalence specific to critical Boltzmann maps; that would require a model-specific argument.
proof_text: Take any probability space with the trivial filtration and T=1. The event {T=1} is certain and all other {T=n+1} events are empty. Taking conditional probabilities gives p_0=1 and p_n=0 for n>=1. Summing proves the assertion. A conditional Borel-Cantelli sufficiency statement cannot supply the converse from this example.
assumptions: Hazards refer to discovery of one fixed target and are stopped at its discovery
limitations: A generic counterexample only. It supplies no critical weight sequence whose map is or is not exhausted.

label: proof
title: Exact truncated expectation and infinite full expectation for exponential decoration growth
statement: For Poisson heights of intensity z*exp(-alpha*h) dh, with z>=0 finite and alpha>0, and independent identically distributed nonnegative decoration marks K(s), the truncated sum S_t^H=sum_(-t<=h_i<=H) K_i(t+h_i), H>=-t, has expectation z*exp(alpha*t)*integral_0^(t+H) exp(-alpha*s)*E K(s) ds. If z>0 and exp(-alpha*s)*E K(s)->c>0, the full sum over h_i>=-t has infinite expectation for each fixed t. With E K(s)=exp(alpha*s), the truncated mean is exactly z*exp(alpha*t)*(t+H).
proof_text: For a nonnegative marked-Poisson integral, Tonelli and the Poisson first-moment identity give E S_t^H=z*integral_(-t)^H exp(-alpha*h)*E K(t+h) dh, allowing either side to be infinite. Put s=t+h to obtain the displayed identity with exp(-alpha*s), not exp(+alpha*s). Sending H to infinity and applying monotone convergence gives the full expectation z*exp(alpha*t)*integral_0^infinity exp(-alpha*s)*E K(s) ds. A strictly positive limiting integrand makes this integral diverge. The special exponential mark makes the integrand identically one, proving the exact truncated formula.
assumptions: A marked Poisson process with the displayed intensity
Nonnegative measurable marks independent of the height process
alpha>0 and H>=-t
limitations: Infinite expectation does not imply an infinite realized sum: only finitely many heights exceed -t almost surely, and finite decorations can yield a finite realized total. No DGFF decoration moment asymptotic is proved here.

label: proof
title: Verified founding-rate bound at the critical immigration parameter
statement: In the Aldous-Huang max-influence city model on the unit square, with alpha=1, beta>0 and c0>0, let M_t be the number of cities and let their positive populations sum to t. With I(y,t)=c0*max_i N_i(t)*|y-x_i|^(-beta), a uniform new arrival founds a city with probability 1/(1+I(y,t)). Its conditional founding probability is at least 1/[2*(1+K*t*M_t^d)], where d=max(beta/2-1,0) and K=(2*pi)^(beta/2)*c0. Consequently almost surely liminf M_t/(log t)^(min(1,2/beta))>0. This includes the boundary beta=2 and beta<2 as well as beta>2.
proof_text: For u>0 the set {y:I(y,t)>u} is contained in the union of M_t disks, the ith having area pi*(c0*N_i/u)^(2/beta). Clipping to the unit square and disk overlap only reduce the area. Put q=2/beta>0. If q<=1, concavity gives sum_i N_i^q<=M_t^(1-q)*t^q. If q>=1, each N_i/t is in [0,1], so sum_i (N_i/t)^q<=sum_i N_i/t=1. Together these give sum_i N_i^q<=M_t^max(1-q,0)*t^q. Thus the area is at most pi*(c0/u)^q*M_t^max(1-q,0)*t^q. Choose u=K*t*M_t^max(beta/2-1,0). Substitution makes this bound exactly 1/2. On the complement, the founding chance is at least 1/(1+u). Integrating over the uniform arrival position yields the displayed lower bound. The new-city indicator changes M_t by one, while a join changes it by zero, so the conditional count-process lemma, whose proof also holds for d=0, applies. Its exponent 1/(d+1) is min(1,2/beta), giving the stated almost sure lower bound. The cached primary paper, Section 2, equations (1)-(3) and rules (i)-(ii), explicitly defines the max influence and founding probability and permits alpha=1.
assumptions: The unit-square max-influence model defined above
alpha=1 and beta>0
A uniform arrival at each integer step and total population t
c0>0 is fixed
limitations: This gives a lower logarithmic city-count order, not a matching upper bound, a limiting constant, or balanced city population sizes. Independent audit is pending.
